html:
The Otoe-Missouria are a Siouan people formed from two related tribes, the Otoe and the Missouria. Today the Otoe-Missouria Tribe has its seat at Red Rock in north central Oklahoma, the area this map territory marks.

In 1492 their ancestors were not in Oklahoma. They lived further north and east, along the lower Missouri River and in what is now Iowa and Missouri, farming maize in river valleys and hunting bison. The Missouria were badly weakened by disease and war in the 1700s and joined the Otoe. In 1804 the Lewis and Clark Expedition held a council with them near present Council Bluffs. Treaties took their land, and in 1881 they were moved to Indian Territory, now Oklahoma. Their kin include the Ioway, who speak almost the same Chiwere language.
